'''Hans Joachim Müller-Eberhard''' (born Hans Joachim Müller, 5 May 1927, [[Magdeburg]]<ref name = nas>{{cite book | url = https://nap.nationalacademies.org/read/10169/chapter/15 | title= Hans Joachim Müller-Eberhard| work = National Academy of Sciences Biographical Memoirs: Volume 79 (2001)| date= 2001| doi= 10.17226/10169| isbn= 978-0-309-07572-5}}</ref> was a distinguished molecular [[immunologist]] who did pioneering research in the United States and his native Germany. The areas of investigation upon which he left his mark include the [[immunoglobulin]]s and the [[complement (biology)|complement]] system.<ref name=nyt>{{cite news
|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/03/07/us/hans-muller-eberhard-70-immunologist-dies.html
|title=Hans Muller-Eberhard, 70, Immunologist, Dies
|last=Burkhart
|first=Ford
|date=March 7, 1998
|work=The New York Times
|accessdate=April 22, 2012}}</ref> Awarded the gold [[Robert Koch Prize]] in 1987. Honorary Member of the Scandinavian Society for Immunology (1973).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.scandinavianimmunology.nu/Honorary-Members.html |title=Honorary Members |access-date=2017-10-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171010210724/http://www.scandinavianimmunology.nu/Honorary-Members.html |archive-date=2017-10-10 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He died on 3 March 1998 in [[Houston]], Texas.<ref name = nyt/>

==Education and career==
Müller-Eberhard studied medicine at the [[University of Göttingen]].<ref name = nas/> He spent three years with [[Henry G. Kunkel]] at the [[Rockefeller University]], where he became interested in immunological research, and investigated γ-globulin.<ref name = nas/><ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1126/science.162.3859.1281 | title = Human Monocytes: Distinct Receptor Sites for the Third Component of Complement and for Immunoglobulin G|first1 = Heinz|last1 =Huber|first2 =Margaret J.|last2 = Polley|first3=William D.|last3 =Linscott|first4 = H. Hugh|last4 = Fudenberg|first5 =Hans J.|last5 = Müller-Eberhard|journal = Science | year = 1968|volume= 162|number = 3859|pages = 1281–1283
| pmid = 4177339}}</ref> Later he worked at [[Uppsala University]] with Gunnar Wallanius on the complement system,<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1146/annurev.bi.57.070188.001541| title = Molecular organization and function of the complement system|journal=Annual Review of Biochemistry|first = H.J.|last = Müller-Eberhard|year = 1988|volume = 57|pages =321–347| pmid = 3052276}}</ref> and obtained his doctorate there.<ref name = nas/> He returned to Rockefeller University to resume work with Kunkel.<ref name = nas/> After six years in the Kunkel laboratory, he was recruited by Frank Dixon to join the [[Scripps Clinic and Research Foundation]] in [[La Jolla]], where he was appointed to the Cecil H. and Ida M. Green Chair in Medical Research in 1972. After problems at Scripps he returned to Germany, at the [[Bernhard Nocht Institute for Tropical Medicine]].
